body:
This changes the behavior in a specific edge case with repeating text.
ex:
`# hahahahaha` with the caret after the very first `h`, searching `hah` forwards will select `# ha[hah]ahaha` where before it selected `# haha[hah]aha`.

However, it is possible to to find these anyway when searching backwards, and it is not necessarily incorrect behavior.
So this is just something to be aware of.
I don't think this is needed, this function is only available to TextEdit and it is only called in one place and it has its own bounds check.

Interesting observation! I just played around with your example in `master` and this PR, and think the new behavior makes more sense to me? But notably CLion (my code editor) seems to match the new behavior. I've never tested it in that much detail, but funnily enough, in both my and CLions implementation, the first round of searches finds every odd `hah` while the second finds the even numbered `hah` (never both).

It would be possible to change it back, if desirable. But I guess it isn't wrong to err on the side of established software.

Edit: lol, I accidentally left the `hahahahah` in one of my pushes. Would have been funny to find on code review

Alright, I guess I was a little overzealous with this change. I removed the check; it will as before crash on invalid access now. With the `subscript[]` operator I just stayed agnostic and kept the check intact.
